coverage_review.verdict:
Every work package in A-D is covered by at least one matrix row; none is skipped. The 18 uncovered items are cross-cutting sections that the topic slices passed over: diagnosis and kill tables, the hypothesis register, open owner decisions, audit-limit lists, a few single acceptance-test rows, the C WP2 label-factory binaries, and D WP8.5.

The one finding that changes the plan is about status, not coverage. The ceiling gate (C G0 / D O-S2) was measured in H470 and did not pass: profile_oracle minus R_none has CI [-0.0091, +0.0212], and R_oracle64 minus R_dope has CI [-0.0001, +0.0204]. The panel's own minimum detectable effect is 0.060 against a 0.01 target, so the result is a fail that is also underpowered. The pretrained-vs-random-router and DOPE-vs-none contrasts also include zero. The matrix labels V1-07 and V1EP-04 DONE_MEASURED, which hides this. Nothing in the DOPE lane records the consequence: wp10_readiness_manifest.json still reads gated_awaiting_dedicated_cluster and has no ceiling gate among its launch gates.

Two follow-ups from that study are also unrecorded:
- H470 found median 0.094 token drift in the unauthenticated tokens_cache.pt used by H452-H469; no note marking those results stale was found, and h475 still opens that cache by path.
- The lm48 audit confirmed a mis-specified transform (SVD coordinates reshaped as 16x3 triples) that is still in the serving code.

One item the documents flagged as missing is now resolved: CutSeedProvider / run_with_seed_provider (B s15) exists in JopeDime crates/jope-pipeline/src/lib.rs:79.

Where A-D conflict with the later documents and today's owner decisions (fidelity-first, CPU-first, the packet is the encoding), the later ones win. Most uncovered v1 items are therefore P2/P3 bookkeeping, except the P1 items that affect how existing evidence is read.

topics.summary: All repo paths below are relative to /home/ubuntu/dope/.agent/worktrees/integration (HEAD 7bbb6f34) unless absolute. The documents ask for one Rust scoreboard (engine/dope-arena plus reducers in engine/dope-core/src/dvs) that scores every generator against a second real sample: roles A/B/C/T/P, unclipped retention and paired harm, kappa for pred/lift/calib/driver calibrated at the 95th percentile of a real control C, realism and disclosure gates, table-level pass coverage with every failure in the denominator, three levels of statistics (10,000-replicate per-artifact simultaneous bounds on at least 200 entities, 10/20/40 replicate escalation, family-clustered Holm comparison), locked panels (POC-9, Quick-24, Dev-120, Stress-12, sealed about 90 families), an 8-to-11-arm swap ladder, official baselines with +T arms, and a hash-frozen contract. About 3,170 lines of Rust exist for this (10 reducer modules, 7 arena modules, 9 tests) and cover roughly half of the formulas in simplified form. None of it has produced a number on real data: evaluate_v3 is reached only from tests and the unused `dope-arena reduce` path, build_schedule and append_cell have no callers, and no panel file, ledger file or v3 receipt exists anywhere. Every coverage figure on the dashboard and in CHANGELOG/agent_chat comes from research/levels/s3_kpi_evaluator.py, a Python stand-in with different and weaker definitions (2 auditors, 40 boosting iterations, a point-estimate parity rule at 0.03, a 24-tree random-forest C2ST against T on at most 180 rows, MIA limit 0.60, ungrouped coefficient Spearman as the driver number), yet the dashboard labels it "Fidelity/v3 Hard-Gate Coverages". kappa* is never calibrated: the reducer hard-codes 1.25 for all four properties, which is stricter than the documents' own real-versus-real q95 for lift (1.86) and calib (1.59), so a real sample would fail it. The per-artifact qualification procedure, the insufficient-evidence verdict, replicate escalation, table-level and worst-family aggregation, the C / bootstrap / compressed-rows references, the sealed panel, the power analysis and gate G1 are absent. The only live engine measurement (0.60-0.64 median retention on 22 tables, one seed, producer script not in the repo) is far from the 0.90 worst-family retention G1 expects the Arena to reproduce, and that discrepancy is unexplained.
top_gaps: No dope-fidelity/v3 number has ever been computed: the Rust reducers and the arena are reached only from tests, while every published coverage comes from research/levels/s3_kpi_evaluator.py with different and weaker definitions (40-iteration boosting, point parity rule at 0.03, 24-tree random-forest C2ST against T, MIA limit 0.60, ungrouped driver Spearman) and is labelled 'Fidelity/v3' on the dashboard (V3-15, V3-16).

There is no run loop or bundle producer: build_schedule and append_cell have no callers, nothing turns auditor output into a PredictionBundle, and no panel lock, ledger or receipt file exists, so the scoreboard cannot be executed even on one table (V3-14, V3-17, V3-18).

Real-versus-real calibration is absent: the C control arm and bootstrap reference are never produced, kappa* is hard-coded to 1.25 for every property (below the documents' own real q95 of 1.86 for lift and 1.59 for calib), realism has no real-vs-real reference, and the contract is an unfrozen candidate that no code reads (V3-05, V3-20, V3-24).

The statistics that turn measurements into verdicts are missing: no table-level or worst-family pass rule, no simultaneous-bound per-artifact qualification with an insufficient-evidence outcome, no >= 200-entity guard, no 10/20/40 replicate escalation, the Holm comparison is unexposed, and nothing validates the bootstrap's false-pass rate (V3-10, V3-11, V3-12, V3-13).

topics.summary: Path shorthand: R/ = /home/ubuntu/dope/.agent/worktrees/integration/ (read at HEAD 7bbb6f34). The documents ask for three named emissions from one packet (faithful or 'standard', distill, matched), an n_fit-driven row policy, and a stateless row-addressable sampler whose rows are identical under any batch size, chunking or thread count, with shared random numbers across candidate packets and no batch statistic, forced class or fitting at sampling time. The Format-1 Rust path implements most of this (R/engine/dope-core/src/sample/emit.rs, SHA-256 row keys in rng.rs) and has four contract tests, but only chunk/offset invariance is tested and nothing is measured. The Format-2 path, which is the v2 engine product, ignores row_offset, namespace and group id, and its 'distill' mode emits two independent sampled draws with weight 1.0 each, so weights per pair_id sum to 2.0, the opposite of the spec. Both neural samplers (DopeSingleEncV6 and DopeFidelityV5) standardise over the batch and draw from a stateful generator, and the Python evaluator forces class presence with a batch-quantile threshold and samples at max(2n, 256) rows; V5 also needs the raw fit rows and fits its label model at sampling time. So every number on the dashboard comes from a sampler outside the contract. No recorded result names its emission or row count; the arena swap ladder labels arms 'matched_1n' and 'faithful_4n' but calls the legacy sampler on Format-1 fits. Gate G3 (+0.02 faithful over matched), the row curve S3-1, the choice of r and the QMC test S3-2/G9d have never been run. The decisive gaps are a conforming neural/packet sampler, a correct Format-2 distill and offset path, and emission-labelled measurements at n and 4n.

topics.summary: The documents ask for a typed per-column law: decimal lattice detected on the raw column (coarsest q0 in {1,2,2.5,5}x10^d, >= 99.5% on grid, 2e-3 tolerance, f32-aware), heaping masses, atoms (<= 32, count >= max(k, 0.005n), >= 3x expectation), tier supports 24/64/256, k-th order-statistic tails with W1 knots, missing as a state, the same for targets, and canonical bit-identical emission. The gate is MargAUC <= 0.60 on >= 90% of Quick-24/dev tables, median feature C2ST down >= 0.10 versus engine 1.3.0 (0.987, with 0.837 expected from a decimal snap alone), retention and privacy unchanged. The repo has a real implementation, ColumnMarginalV2 (engine/dope-core/src/marginal/{v2,lattice,atoms,tails}.rs), wired into the Format-2 CATF pipeline and binary codec, with five synthetic unit tests. The decisive defect is that the pipeline fits it on model-space values (schema.to_model output), not raw values, so a raw decimal grid becomes a 1/N step the detector's candidate set matches only by coincidence; the unit tests pass because they feed raw planted columns directly. Emission then goes through an affine/exp_m1 inverse and 6-decimal formatting, there is no decimal round-trip test, regression targets get no lattice or atom treatment, and heaping keeps one multiple against a uniform expectation. No gate is measured: the only recorded realism numbers are C2ST 0.934 (v1.3.1) and 0.9045 (v2.0.0) on 22 tables from a Python RF evaluator, a drop of 0.03 against the required 0.10, with regression and binary retention falling. The measuring instruments are too coarse to see the defect: Rust MargAUC is a <= 32 quantile-bin histogram ratio, native C2ST trees split on 7 octile thresholds, and the Python MargAUC is a median rank AUC over the first 12 columns. The neural side is further away: DopeSingleEncV6 decodes every column as a 17-knot continuous spline (C2ST 0.999 per agent_chat.md) and DopeFidelityV5 copies sorted raw fit values for discrete columns. Nothing in this slice was executed; all statuses come from reading code at HEAD 7bbb6f34 and recorded result files.

M16: none of the three realism instruments (Rust <= 32-bin MargAUC, Rust octile-threshold C2ST, Python rank-AUC median over 12 columns) can see on-grid versus off-grid values, and none reports a real-vs-real reference, so G3/G4 cannot be certified or falsified today.

topics.summary: The documents ask for a cross-fitted teacher stack (K=5, stack weights and calibration fitted inside each fold's complement, poison-tested), a student distilled onto real rows plus min(8n, 200,000) teacher-labelled probes and grown to the byte budget rather than cut at a noisy validation minimum, a direct-label control at equal bytes, noise refitted on untouched real labels, faithful/distill emission, a Max tier, and gate G2/G5 (+0.03 at n and +0.02 at 4n over engine 1.3, student >= 0.97 of teacher, at least half the cap used). A simplified version of the whole chain exists in Rust under /home/ubuntu/dope/.agent/worktrees/integration/engine/dope-core/src (teacher/, distil/, forest/soft_boost.rs, compile/v2/pipeline.rs) and is reachable through `dope fit --format 2`. None of it is measured against its gate: there is no Quick-24 panel, no engine-1.3 baseline on the same tables, and no record of teacher quality, student retention of teacher or bytes used. The only numbers are two single-row arena files on 22 tables from an evaluator whose source is not in the repo: median 0.6024 -> 0.6393 after commit 3de9035c, with binary 0.1529 -> 0.0845, regression 0.9004 -> 0.8374 and parity 0.2727 -> 0.2273, far from the tips' 0.98-0.995. That commit rewrote the linear teacher member as cyclic coordinate Newton, stratified folds by label, mined pairs on residuals, fixed main-effect purification, truncated the student to its best probe tree and added byte-cap binary search with temperature refit. The stratification makes fold assignment label-dependent, and the poison test the specs require is not actually implemented. Decisive gaps: no gate measurement or attribution, no direct-label control or SELECT-based choice, capacity hard-capped well below the budget (probes <= 4,096, teacher boosters <= 80 trees, student <= 600 trees at depth <= 5 in half the budget), leakage proof not established, and Format 2 distill emission and `dope predict` not delivered. LearningSignatureV1 is an in-sample diagnostic that departs from the E section 15 schema and changes nothing in the packet; F section 9's learned sketch encoder is superseded by H.
top_gaps: Gate G2/G5 has never been measured and the only evidence runs against it: Format 2 scores median 0.6393 (mean 0.2217, binary 0.0845, regression 0.8374, parity 0.2273) on 22 tables from an evaluator not in the repo, with no engine-1.3 baseline on the same tables, no worst-family metric and no intervals (T19).

No attribution exists: teacher quality, student retention of teacher, bytes used and stop reason are not computed or reported, and the S5.0 experiment was skipped, so it is unknown whether the teacher, the student trainer, capacity or the covariate model causes the shortfall (T01, T18).

There is no direct-label control, no teacher-weight candidates, no `--teacher off`, and SELECT labels are never read, so the kill rule 'ship the control if distillation does not win at equal bytes' cannot be applied and a weak teacher is distilled unconditionally (T13, T14).

Capacity is hard-capped far below 'fill the budget': at most 4,096 probes instead of min(8n, 200,000), teacher boosters at most 80 trees, student at most 600 depth-5 trees in half the budget even at Max, and main and pair stages fitted by least squares on clamped logits (T02, T08, T10, T17).

Leakage safety is asserted but not proven: the poison test does not poison a fold, fold assignment and the agreement scale depend on labels, teacher-auditor independence is not enforced, and the external seam is ingest-only with an unchecked split hash and a zero-target hazard when probe predictions are missing (T03, T04, T06, T07).

Anchor for discrete and nominal columns: I P6b uses the marginal as base with no Gaussian offset; H W4.B uses a copula offset plus pooling of levels under k; G S6b adds a polychoric candidate. The repo follows H with moment calibration. Prefer H, and keep I's marginal-base as a candidate chosen by held-out likelihood.

Anchor regime: H 5.2/C.4 anchors on the regime-mixture copula; I P6b and G A.3 specify the single-regime copula. The repo is single-regime. Unresolved; decide by a likelihood comparison once the ablation arms exist.

Gate name and thresholds: H calls it G4, G and I call it G6. Rule violations: within 0.01 of B (H) versus <= 2x real (I, G). Driver: within 0.05 of the twin (H) versus gap <= 0.03 (G). G gates nearest-record share <= 0.55; H's pilot shows that would reject the chain on 10-11 of 13 tables and says to calibrate it and let membership inference decide. Prefer H.

Kill rule: H (anchored trees at Max must beat copula + columns + rules on worst-family retention and realism), G (C2ST gain < 0.05 at 64 KiB after two tuning rounds, or privacy fails on > 5% at k = 10), I (privacy fails after raising k and leaf floors twice). The fallbacks also differ: copula + rules (H), calibration + discrete estimate + rules (G), regimes + rules + joint missingness (I).

Shrinkage and leaf floors: G alpha = 20 with leaves >= max(k, 0.5% n); H alpha in {5, 20, 100} with leaves >= k and capacity by rounds; E alpha = 2 from {0, 0.5, 2, 20} as a mixture with the global law, min leaf 30, depth <= 3. H says leaf size is not the memorisation control.

Generator family: E 13.1-13.4 specifies a stand-alone typed density-tree challenger with histogram and affine/residual leaves, and F 8.2.1 a Chow-Liu typed tree; G, H and I use a tree residual on the copula. H B.5 resolves to the anchored model with E's predicates, shrinkage and lookahead.

Rule mining data and grammar: H mines on BUILD and confirms on SELECT with binary operators; I mines on fit rows only, adds a not-implied-by-marginals test and three-parent arithmetic forms. E limits approximate relations to 64 candidates and 16 accepted and requires the exception law to be a restricted mixture component. Take H's roles with I's grammar and E's accounting.
Where the target and mask sit: F 7.4 factorises Q(M) Q(X|M) Q(Y|X,M); G, H and I interleave each column's missing state in the chain and sample the target last from the student.

topics.summary: Path shorthand: ENG = /home/ubuntu/dope/.agent/worktrees/integration/engine/dope-core (HEAD 7bbb6f34, read-only; nothing was built or run). The documents (H W4 + C.4/C.5, I P6/P7d, G S6, E 13/16, F 7.4/8) ask for a BUILD/SELECT-confirmed rule miner (FD, ARITH, BIN, INEQ, EXCL, MISS), a copula-anchored autoregressive tree layer with missingness as a chain state, zero-byte copula moment calibration, an owner-side entropy-balanced projection compiled back into the sampler, and a gate of median C2ST <= 0.70 that is never worse than copula-only, plus rule, driver, kappa and privacy conditions. A real first version of nearly all of this exists in Rust (ENG/src/structure, ENG/src/catf, ENG/src/copula.rs, ENG/src/compile/v2/project.rs) and is wired into fit_v2 and the Format 2 sampler, with five behavioural tests in ENG/tests/structure_catf.rs. None of the spec gates has been run: there is no Quick-24/dev-120 run, no copula-only / rules-only / CATF ablation arm, and CATF is hard-wired rather than chosen by a selector. The only measurement is one 22-table line from a Python evaluator that is not in the repo: /home/ubuntu/dope-data/arena/rust_format2_v200/eval.jsonl reports c2st_auc_median 0.9045 (gate 0.70), realism_coverage 0.25, privacy_pass_coverage 0.5357 (gate 0.95). That matches H's own pilot, where an 8-round chain scored 0.886 and a 40-round chain 0.641: the repo caps CATF at 2/4/8 trees per column and stops on in-sample likelihood. The rule layer is weaker than its names suggest: ARITH is linear only, INEQ and EXCL are post-hoc overwrites, MISS is one-directional, and the violation metric skips FD-2 and BIN. The moment projection is computed as a diagnostic and never compiled into the packet. The artifact the owner now calls "the encoding" (DopeSingleEncV6, <= 2 KiB) has no rules, no tree layer and no applied missingness, and Format 2's CATF section cannot fit 2 KiB as encoded.
top_gaps: The joint-structure gate has never been run and there are no ablation arms (JS-19, JS-20). INEQ and EXCL are post-hoc overwrites that the documents forbid. MISS is one-directional. The violation metric skips FD-2 and BIN, and rule scans stop at 48 columns.

The owner-side moment projection is a diagnostic, not a compile step (JS-15). Weights are discarded, compile_projected_sampler has no callers, and no fitter accepts weights. H measured +0.029 worst-family retention and parity on 10 of 13 tables instead of 6 from this operator.

topics.summary: Path shorthand used below: ENG = /home/ubuntu/dope/.agent/worktrees/integration/engine/dope-core (lane HEAD 7bbb6f34). The documents ask for a bounded compiler that splits the owner's rows into BUILD/SELECT before fitting, audits every candidate on its exact decoded bytes with native learners, proposes seven increments ranked by gain per byte, orders candidates by fixed lexicographic buckets, enforces fit and audit budgets, picks with a clean two-learner selector, ships nested prefix tiers with carry-forward, refits the frozen recipe on all rows with lineage, and attaches a small certificate. What exists is a set of leaf utilities: a role splitter, a transitive bucket comparator, a carry-forward resolver, a damped-Newton tilt solver, a ridge distance and a 115-line generic loop skeleton. Only ENG/tests/compiler_v2.rs calls the loop, the comparator and the carry-forward resolver, and it feeds them hand-written scores and dummy byte vectors. The shipped Format 2 path (`fit_v2`, ENG/src/compile/v2/pipeline.rs:153-436) is a single fixed pass: capacity comes from a budget lookup table, no candidate is ever scored on SELECT, the P+ weights are computed and discarded, one tier entry is written, and the artifact is the BUILD-only fit (about 64% of rows) while recording n_fit as all rows. None of the gates has a recorded measurement: G5/G7 closed loop versus fixed allocation, selector regret <= 0.01, zero tier drops > 0.005, certificate error <= 0.03, compile <= 20 minutes at 20,000 x 20 on 32 threads, 36 of 36 reruns identical, fast within 0.01 of standard. The only Format 2 numbers on disk are two single-line files (/home/ubuntu/dope-data/arena/rust_format2_v131/eval.jsonl and rust_format2_v200/eval.jsonl: median retention 0.6024 and 0.6393 on 22 tables), with no tier, budget, timing or rerun dimension. The decisive gaps are therefore the missing auditor and proposal generators, the missing final refit on all rows, the absent selector and tier machinery in the product path, and the absence of any gate harness (rerun probe, compile-time benchmark, regret and tier-inversion probes).
top_gaps: The closed loop does not exist in the product path: loop_driver.rs is a 115-line generic fold called only by a test with dummy byte vectors, there is no exact-artifact auditor and no proposal generator, and fit_v2 is a single fixed pass (CL-02, CL-03, CL-04). Every G5/G7 gate is therefore unrunnable.

The shipped Format 2 artifact is the BUILD-only fit (about 64% of rows) with no refit on all rows, and it records n_fit as 100% of rows (CL-11). This is the cheapest change with a direct expected fidelity effect and it also fixes a mislabelled quantity.

No selector and no tier machinery for Format 2: each byte budget is an independent compile from a lookup table, one tier entry is written, carry-forward is never invoked, and neither selector regret (<= 0.01) nor tier drops (> 0.005) has been measured (CL-09, CL-10).

No gate harness: no rerun probe for 36 of 36, no thread-count determinism test for fit_v2, no compile-time or RSS record, no size-versus-fidelity curve at 0.5-4 KiB, no frozen dev panel or excluded-auditor protocol (CL-16, CL-17, CL-18, CL-21).

P+ projection and the certificate are diagnostics with misleading labels: weights are discarded, gap (4) is reported as equal to gap (3) by default, the report field ridge_cert_relative_risk holds an RMSE difference, and there is no certificate section or measured certificate error (CL-13, CL-15).

The driver performs none of these steps (it delegates to a closure, lines 88-101), accepts every under-cap candidate, and SELECT is by specification exposed, not sealed.

The loop test feeds vec![step as u8; sz] byte vectors and constant scores (lines 156-176); no real artifact is compiled or audited. The ladder has four gap fields, gap_decoded defaults to gap_compiled (line 155), and 'compiled' is a systematic resample of pool indices, not a refitted sampler.

engine/dope-core/src/compile/v2/pipeline.rs:1-6 module header lists 'P+ damped-Newton projection + ridge_certificate -> Format 2 binary encode' as part of the wired pipeline and cites G-01, G-02, G-05; the projection does not alter the encoded program and no gate measurement exists.

FitV2Report.ridge_cert_relative_risk (pipeline.rs:78, 428) holds RidgeCertificate.pred_rmse_diff, which is not a relative risk; the packet's n_fit (pipeline.rs:362) is the full row count although CATF, teacher and student are fitted on BUILD rows only.

disagreements_between_documents: Container identity and layout: E reserves DPS1 (64 B header, 32 B directory, SHA-256 digest, 11 section tags); H specifies DX1 with the same header/directory under a new dx1/ module; I and G call it format 2 of .dope. The repo built 'DOPE2' with a 32 B header and one body CRC. Prefer I/G naming (matches the repo) with H's validation rules; H's fixed 64 B + 32 B per section costs about 352 B for nine sections, 17% of a 2 KiB cap, so the layout needs an owner call.

Tiers: I and G make a tier a physical prefix of an increment list with truncate(bytes, tier) and gate G9 'prefix truncation equals a direct compile'; H (newest) and E write a complete file per tier first and allow physical prefixes only after a measured saving (G7b). Prefer H; I's G9 prefix clause becomes conditional.

Where the claim is made: I and G put the fidelity claim at Max (G: 1 MiB ceiling, decision O-5; I: Max bounded by admission limit and a >= 1% per doubling plateau rule) and the per-byte claim on 2/4/16/64 KiB; H headlines parity coverage per tier at 4/16/64 KiB and max (2 MiB in dev); F proposes 2, 4, 16, 64, 256 KiB, 1 MiB plus a generous-capacity control. The owner decision (<= 2 KiB headline, 0.5-4 KiB curve) overrides all four.

Entropy coder trigger: G R6 (payload >= 90% of cap on >= 25% of tables), I P9 (only if framing rather than modelling separates DOPE from compressed rows at 2-4 KiB), H G7b (measured byte saving at equal audit scores), E (rANS deferred until complete packets are correct). All defer; the triggers differ.

Privacy thresholds: G uses nearest-record share 0.50 +/- 0.05 and exact-match rate <= the A-vs-B rate plus sampling error; H uses exact-match excess <= 0.01 and a nearest-record bound calibrated on dev; E forbids carrying over 0.5-style thresholds from unequal reference sizes and labels the profile diagnostic until calibrated. The repo hard-codes 0.55 and 0.005.
Privacy gate panel and tier: G dev-120 at 64 KiB and at Max with G6 intact; H dev tables at 64 KiB with G4 intact; I Quick-24 at 64 KiB with G6 intact. Strictest is G.

Back-off order: I (raise k and leaf floors, lower tilt clip, drop audit rounds, raise noise floor); H (anchored trees, then atoms, then rules); G (raise k, shrink tree depth on small tables). The repo truncates tree fractions only.

Scaling: I and G define one NC2 recipe (I: asinh guard and 0.5%-99.5% bulk; G: affine between k-th order statistics with 2%/96%/2%); H defines two views, unit-linear and unit-rank; I makes the unit space under one frozen card the evaluation space, while F 7.3 and E 12.2 keep the canonical NC1-style coordinates as the benchmark space and allow smarter transforms only internally and only after a measured bottleneck.

Embed view: I samples 4,096 rows and runs the existing 629-D extractor, with PacketFeaturesV2 as a packet-computed view; H defines a new fixed-length vector (certificate, column summaries, copula spectrum, probe responses, hashed sketch) plus the 4,096-row compatibility path; G describes landmark scalars, teacher metrics and structural statistics. The owner's '64/128-D prefix of the packet = the embedding' matches none of them exactly.

Quantisation timing: G (R6, T15) and E defer quantisation tricks until a tier is byte-bound and start from f64 reference arrays; I's G9 and H's W5 finalisation expect measured bit widths in the first release (H: 6-bit leaves, discrete supports 24/64/256 at 4/16/64 KiB).

topics.summary: All repo paths below are relative to /home/ubuntu/dope/.agent/worktrees/integration (HEAD 7bbb6f34). The documents ask for one source-free packet (format 2 of .dope, called DX1 in H and DPS1 in E) that carries only positional/unit-space information, is byte-accounted as a whole file, is quantised by measured harm per byte, passes empirical disclosure gates inside the compile loop on >= 95% of dev tables, and serves sample / predict / embed / audit card, with JopeDime's 629-D vector becoming a function of that packet. A Format 2 container, section codecs, an NC2 scale card, a privacy reducer, a back-off ladder, PacketFeaturesV2 and a 629 "bridge" all exist in Rust and have unit tests, but none of the topic's gates (I G8/G9, H G7/G7a/G7b, G G8) is DONE_MEASURED. The decisive gaps: (1) the packet writes column names, category strings and f64 lo/hi into its schema section by default, the opposite of every document's hidden-information rule; (2) the byte cap is not enforced (an over-budget zero-tree packet is returned as Ok), no per-section ledger exists and no Format 2 packet size on a real table is recorded anywhere; (3) the in-loop privacy back-off is fail-open, asserts rather than measures k-support, plants no canary, records no trace, and the only measured privacy pass coverage is 0.46-0.54 against a 0.95 gate; (4) Q16 quantisation, the tier table, truncate and carry-forward are declared but unwired (all nine sections are CODEC_RAW, one tier entry, hard-coded f32 and 8-bit leaves); (5) dope embed returns a stored 32-float owner summary and the 629 bridge returns column means/stds, so nothing JopeDime consumes is a function of the packet. NC2 is implemented as a library with one test and has no caller, so its non-inferiority gate has never run and NC1 correctly remains the default. The owner decision (headline at <= 2 KiB, 0.5-4 KiB curve) moves the claim from the documents' Max/64 KiB end of the grid to its smallest point, which turns the documents' deferred items (bit allocation, entropy coding, framing overhead, feasibility refusals, B_cold of any shared decoder) into first-order work.
top_gaps: No zero-raw-row packet has a measured size or a measured fidelity point at the owner's <= 2 KiB headline: format-2 eval rows carry no bytes, V6 bytes are a formula that excludes a shared decoder, fit_v2 has no sub-8 KiB capacity plan, and the cap is not enforced (pipeline.rs:376-399 returns an over-budget packet as Ok). PK-04, PK-06, PK-07.

The packet discloses what every document says must stay with the owner: column names, category strings and f64 lo/hi are written into the schema section by default and the inverse scale travels even under --anonymize (format2_bin.rs:142-158). The NC2 public-schema/private-card split that would fix it exists but has no caller. PK-12, PK-14.

Privacy in the loop is not a gate: reducer errors become pass:true, k is asserted not measured, no canary is planted, no trace is recorded, the ladder emits its last step even when it fails, and the only measured privacy pass coverage is 0.4643 / 0.5357 against a >= 0.95 requirement. PK-17, PK-18, PK-19.

Quantisation, tier prefixes and carry-forward are declared but unwired (all sections CODEC_RAW, one tier entry, no truncate, resolve_carry_forward_tiers used only in tests; f32 and 8-bit choices hard-coded without measurement). disagreements_between_documents: Driver statistic and gate. H (newest): TV distance between grouped importance masses, floor 0.05, H3 = within 0.03 of the B-vs-A value (but H G4 says within 0.05 of the twin's). I: kappa_driver with distance 1 - min(mass, rank), gate UCB90 <= kappa* (q95 of real_fresh). G: 1 - TV reported as a gap, DRIVER = UCB95(D(B) - D(S)) <= 0.03. E: absolute error <= 0.02 null-loss units per group, positive-mass TV <= 0.10, ordering disagreement <= 0.10, and warns against using the synthetic/real over real/real ratio as a target. Recommendation: H's TV definition with I's control-derived threshold as the gate; report G's gap and E's absolute errors beside it.
Permutation repeats: E fixes 10 per group; H and G require >= 6.

Whether a driver mechanism is ever built: I P10 adds effect-curve matching (effect.splines) and permuted-row weight if kappa_driver fails; H drops the ALE correction splines outright and relies on the C+ increment. Both agree nothing is built before a measured gap; prefer H (newest) and treat I's splines as the fallback only on a recorded failure.

Parity definition: I tests mean z(0.98) against A (retention >= 0.98 of the source model, UCB95 <= 0); G tests harm against the fresh twin B (UCB95 <= 0.02 x gain); H uses min_f R_f(S) >= min_f R_f(B) - 0.02 on >= 90% of tables; E uses a simultaneous H_0.95 tier with 0.98 as the demanding tier. The repo implements G's form. I's version was tested on the built engine; H is newest and is twin-relative.

Per-artifact inference: E and H require 10,000 replicates with simultaneous max-T bounds, >= 200 entities and 10/20/40 table-key replicates; G asks only for a paired bootstrap crossed with >= 5 emitted tables and 3 learner seeds; I specifies 2S compiles, 3 (dev) or 5 (confirmation) fit seeds, 3 sample seeds, 3 auditor seeds.

kappa* values: G gives 1.23 / 1.86 / 1.59 (pred / lift / calib) and treats driver as a gap; H gives 1.23 / 1.86 / 1.63 (driver) / 1.59 and separate working gates (kappa_pred median <= 1.00 and <= 1.10 on >= 80% of cells at 4n); I leaves them to Quick-24 calibration.

Realism and disclosure thresholds: C2ST <= 0.65 (H H4) vs <= 0.70 (G, I, H G4); rule violations within 0.01 of B (H) vs within 2x the real rate (G, I); exact-match excess <= 0.01 (H) vs holdout rate + 0.001 (I) vs 'plus sampling error' (G); nearest-record share 'calibrated bound' (H) vs <= 0.55 (I) vs 0.50 +/- 0.05 (G).

Coverage denominator: I keeps failed, missing and undetermined cells in the denominator; G excludes uninformative cells and counts a table with no informative family in no coverage; H counts shares of tables with failures, timeouts and refusals in the denominator. The repo excludes uninformative cells.

Sealed-run design: H: tiers 4/16/64 KiB and max, m in {n, 4n}, faithful; G: same tiers, faithful + distill + matched, sentence evaluated at Max and at <= 64 KiB; I: claim at standard emission and Max tier, frontier on {2, 4, 16, 64, 256 KiB, 1 MiB, Max}. All use 5 data seeds x 3 sample seeds where stated.

Claim sentence content: H: parity coverage vs every authentic and +T baseline, non-inferior H3/H4, V on >= 95%, leads rate track at 16 and 64 KiB. I: highest Parity, Equivalence and Pass Coverage, paired worst-family kappa_pred and T intervals excluding zero, C2ST non-inferior, held-out foundation auditor agrees, Pass Coverage >= rivals and compressed rows up to 64 KiB. G: highest Pass Coverage, better paired parity harm and kappa_pred, not worse on C2ST, driver gap or selection regret.

Baseline roster: H adds TabSDS, a boosted-tree generator and an in-context generator; G adds CTGAN, TVAE, SMOTE; F adds TabNAT, coreset/medoid controls, TDColER/TAME, TabPFN generation; I's development list is shorter (SMOTE, ARF, TabDDPM, TabSyn).

Sealed panel size: E and G plan about 90 source families adjusted by a power analysis before sealing; I derives size only from Dev variance and a declared minimum difference; the repo hard-codes >= 90.

topics.summary: All five v2 documents put the learned lane last: H gates it after G5 (W9, GPU budget D-7 only after G5), G after G7 and owner decision O-7 (R3/R4), I after G5-G7 plus hundreds of logged compiler runs, E only once the conditional-tree ceiling fails, and F only after its first batch (truthful registry, repaired protocol, native joint candidate, ceiling study). The repo is doing the reverse: at HEAD 7bbb6f34 three neural runs are live on four GPUs (dashboard snapshot 19:2xZ) while no scoreboard gate (G0/G1/G5) has a recorded measurement and docs/plans/dope-next and dope-final result notes do not exist. Almost nothing the documents ask of a neural result is measured. The flow_v6 / V5 sampler still reads raw fit rows at sampling time, so its 0.83-0.90 is not an encoding. The zero-raw-row DopeSingleEncV6 scores main KPI -0.08 (step 2100, 672 B formula) and -0.16 (step 850, 1040 B formula) with C2ST 0.9997 / 0.9985, and its "encoding bytes" are an arithmetic formula, never serialised, never natively decoded, and exclude the scale card and shared decoder weights. Both decoders standardise over the sample batch, which breaks the row-addressable one-law rule in H, G and I. Training optimises ridge / IRLS linear proxies plus random Fourier features only; selection uses one 42-46 table panel that also feeds the training curriculum, with a strict '>' on a noisy median and a filename-stem "family" split. Before any neural number may be claimed the documents require: (1) the v3 scoreboard passing G0/G1 with real-vs-real twin references; (2) scoring after serialise, parse and native sample with whole-file bytes and decoder closure counted; (3) a row-local sampler; (4) a held-out learner family and failures kept in denominators; (5) an unexposed confirmation panel; (6) G9c non-inferiority to the closed-loop native compile at equal bytes; (7) a positive scaling curve before a second run. Until a sealed run everything is development_only.
top_gaps: Order inversion (N01, N02): a multi-run neural campaign is live on four GPUs before G0/G1/G5 have any recorded measurement. H W9 is 'after G5' with GPU budget D-7 only after G5; G and I are stricter (after G7). It also sits against today's CPU-first owner rule.

No neural number is an admissible encoding result (N03, N04). The flow_v6 / V5 sampler reads raw fit rows (v5_fidelity_net.py:212-313). V6 bytes are a formula (v6_single_encoding.py:119-120), never serialised or natively decoded, and exclude the scale card and decoder closure. Everything is scored by a weak Python evaluator with no real-vs-real reference.

The one zero-raw-row model is far below the native path, with nothing to judge G9c against (N06, N13). V6 scores -0.08 / -0.16 main KPI with C2ST 0.9997 / 0.9985, against Rust Format 2 at 0.6393 on a different 22-table panel. It decodes every column as continuous, never applies missingness, and trains on soft labels that the evaluator hardens.

Both neural samplers break the one-law, row-addressable rule (N05): batch standardisation at v6_single_encoding.py:185 and v5_fidelity_net.py:234, plus a class-presence fallback at s3_kpi_evaluator.py:292-293.

Selection and exposure (N15, N07, N12): one 42-46 table panel is headline, selector, soup selector and curriculum feedback. Promotion is a strict '>' on a noisy median. The 'family' split is a filename-stem hash. Training optimises linear proxies only, and further runs were launched after a flat scaling curve (0.8937 vs 0.8932).

disagreements_between_documents: Ceiling arm: C uses profile_oracle (own-pool half A scored on half B) against zero; D uses R_oracle64 (pivoted-QR basket of 64 common programs) against R_dope with a registered margin. H470 ran both and both miss; the non-registered 16-program basket passes.

Primary endpoint: A uses a per-task log RMSE ratio with a FIT-mean fallback and a 1% geometric gate; B uses a clipped normalized loss with failure = 10, point >= 0.01 and LCB > 0; C and D keep the historical flywheel utility (-fitness, -2.0 on gate fail) and Elo. A itself says historical utility must not be pooled with the new endpoint. Nothing later adjudicates this; B is the most precise.

Shuffle control: C permutes within fold by a metadata hash; D permutes within fold and adds noise and a 5-seed random router; B requires a cross-family donor permutation with the mapping recorded plus frozen-random and scratch-trained encoders; A requires the consumer to be retrained on the shuffled arm. topics.summary: Path shorthand: WT = /home/ubuntu/dope/.agent/worktrees/integration, CORPUS = /home/ubuntu/dope-data/s3-v250-corpus. The four v1 documents ask for an honestly counted corpus (seven separate counters, exact dedup identity, family closure, a mixture of real/synthetic pools), a bounded streaming trainer (indexed shards, shape-bucketed batches, weighted DDP loss, committed-exposure ledger, exact resume) and a gated ladder 100k -> 1M -> (3M) -> 10M with measured cost. What exists is two disconnected halves: (1) Rust/Python contract code from v1.3.0 (rust/corpus admit(), TrainingViewV1, generator_pilot, transfer_stream.py ExposureLedger/IndexedStream/capture/restore) that is tested on fixtures but is referenced by nothing except its own tests, and (2) the pipeline that actually trains (s3_fast_pipeline.py + s3_ddp_trainer.py on an untracked Python-built corpus) which implements none of those contracts. Distance to the documents' unit: 4,145 real TRAIN tables is 0.041% of 10,000,000 content-distinct bases (a 2,413x shortfall); in D's weaker unit (views) the lost ddp4 run fed about 595,680 episodes (about 144 per table), about 6% of 10M, with no view identity recorded. I measured 0 exact-content duplicates among the 4,598 stored tables (X-only, X+y and a column-order-invariant sketch), but the split is a filename-stem hash, 4,494 of 4,598 tables have licence status unknown, and the builder silently truncates to the first 256 columns. Nothing on the ladder has been run; no rung, no nested-subset comparison, no cost receipt exists in the repo, and wp10_readiness_manifest.json is still gated. The later v2 documents (G R2-R4, H W9, I research lane) move neural training on a prior corpus behind gates G5/G7, so the 10M-scale rows are P3, while the trainer-hygiene rows (resume, ledger, DDP semantics, family split, honest counters) are P0/P1 because a neural model is training today. No row reaches DONE_MEASURED.
top_gaps: Split and family identity (R03, R20): the train/val cut is a filename-stem hash with only two roles; the audit found 62 of 453 val tables with a same-source train sibling, and promotion is an argmax over hundreds of noisy looks on that panel. Every number downstream inherits this.

No resume and no exposure ledger in the pipeline that trains (R18, R17): checkpoints hold EMA weights only, the 4-rank run was lost at step 18,615 of 20,000, and no artifact can show which tables contributed to a checkpoint. Tested reference code (transfer_stream.py, v4_trainer.py) exists but nothing calls it.

Counters (R01, R09, R21): the one published figure, unique_splits_seen, is a by-construction view counter times world_size shown as a uniqueness proof. Real distance to the documents' unit is 4,145 TRAIN bases versus 10,000,000 (0.041%, 2,413x short), sampled 11.4x more often per multiclass table than per regression table, with no family balancing.

No scaling evidence at any rung (R22, R23): nothing on the 100k/1M/10M ladder has run, no nested-subset comparison exists even at 4,145 tables, the only capacity contrast is confounded and flat (0.8937 vs 0.8932), and the repo holds no measured cost model. A CPU mini-ladder is the cheapest way to learn whether more data pays before any generator work.

Training mechanics contradict the streaming spec (R14, R16, R15, R24): one episode per forward, unweighted per-parameter DDP averaging with rank-local step decisions, silent drops of non-finite/OOM episodes, and a corpus builder outside the repo that truncates to the first 256 columns and erases missingness.

topics.summary: Path prefixes: W = /home/ubuntu/dope/.agent/worktrees/integration, J = /home/ubuntu/JopeDime. Documents A-D ask that a new DOPE encoder reach JopeDime only as a new, frozen, SHA-pinned identity with Rust inference parity below 1e-5, a measured latency/memory budget (30 ms GPU median, about 100 ms on 8 CPU threads), a pre-registered transfer benefit (point estimate >= 0.01 with a paired family-bootstrap 95% lower bound > 0, shuffled and frozen-random controls, failure-rate increase < 0.5 pp, slice harm < 0.02), one locked confirmation look, a machine-readable promotion receipt and a rollback pointer. What exists is the incumbent's scaffolding: the ReleasedV1 pin d0b69603 and J/models/dope-compat.json, a same-graph UnqualifiedCandidateV1 guard that refuses relabelling, v3 Python/Rust parity (1.41e-6), freeze guards with composite SHA c51a56d0 equal before and after in H470/H473, a 12-field token-cache key module, a receipt validator, the three corpus schemas and a family bootstrap. None of it has been exercised for a successor: DopeFidelityV5, DopeFlowV6, DopeSingleEncV6 and the Format 2 packet have no graph contract, strict loader, Rust inference, serialized-bytes measurement, latency number, attribution run or receipt instance. The only measured v1 gate is C's G0 on the released encoder (JopeDime H470), and it failed: profile_oracle minus R_none CI [-0.00914, +0.02118], with an instrument MDE of 0.060 against the 0.01 target. By C's own rule that stops surface-A ranking work and redirects to retrieval, zero-shot and DOPE's retention product, so most integration rows are P3 until the owner reopens the track. The decisive gaps are therefore upstream of JopeDime: the headline 0.8978 is not measured through a serialized zero-raw-row artifact, there is no confirmation panel or look ledger, and no successor identity exists. The brief is stale on one point: PR #387 was merged at 2026-11-22T19:04:20Z as feafa4ee (origin/main now equals it) with the required jankurai-audit check failing. No dope-engine-v2.0.0 tag or release exists, and JopeDime still pins dope-engine-v1.3.0.
